claim: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is responsible for folding secretory and membrane proteins.
source: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is responsible for folding secretory and membrane proteins, but disturbed ER proteostasis may lead to protein aggregation and subsequent cellular and clinical pathologies.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about ER function.

claim: Disturbed ER proteostasis may lead to protein aggregation and subsequent cellular and clinical pathologies.
source: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is responsible for folding secretory and membrane proteins, but disturbed ER proteostasis may lead to protein aggregation and subsequent cellular and clinical pathologies.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific understanding and cited literature in the field.

claim: 2-phenylimidazo[2,1-b]benzothiazole derivatives (IBTs) were identified as chemical chaperones in a cell-based high-throughput screen.
source: Here, we identified 2-phenylimidazo[2,1-b]benzothiazole derivatives (IBTs) as chemical chaperones in a cell-based high-throughput screen.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by the HTS data presented in Figure 1.

claim: IBT21 directly binds to unfolded or misfolded proteins.
source: Biochemical and chemical biology approaches revealed that IBT21 directly binds to unfolded or misfolded proteins and inhibits protein aggregation.
evidence: This is supported by photoaffinity labeling experiments and mass spectrometry data presented in Figure 6.

claim: IBT21 inhibits protein aggregation.
source: Biochemical and chemical biology approaches revealed that IBT21 directly binds to unfolded or misfolded proteins and inhibits protein aggregation.
evidence: This is supported by ProteoStat dye assays and in vitro aggregation assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: IBT21 prevented cell death caused by chemically induced ER stress.
source: Finally, IBT21 prevented cell death caused by chemically induced ER stress and by a proteotoxin, an aggression-prone prion protein.
evidence: This is supported by cell viability and proliferation assays shown in Figure 7.

claim: IBT21 prevented cell death caused by an aggression-prone prion protein.
source: Finally, IBT21 prevented cell death caused by chemically induced ER stress and by a proteotoxin, an aggression-prone prion protein.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with mutant prion protein overexpression shown in Figure 7E-G.

claim: The UPR is initiated by the activation of three signal transducers located in the ER: IRE1α, PERK and ATF6.
source: The UPR is initiated by the activation of the following three signal transducers located in the ER: IRE1α, PERK and ATF6.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations (Mori, 2000; Walter and Ron, 2011; Han and Kaufman, 2017).

claim: Disturbance of the UPR has important pathological consequences, including diabetes, neurodegenerative disease and cancer.
source: Disturbance of the UPR has important pathological consequences, including diabetes, neurodegenerative disease and cancer (Hotamisligil, 2010; Martínez et al., 2018; Clarke et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature in the field.

claim: KIRA6, an inhibitor of the UPR regulator IRE1, has shown potent anti-diabetic efficacy.
source: KIRA6, an inhibitor of the UPR regulator IRE1, and azoramide, an ER calcium modulator, have shown potent anti-diabetic efficacy (Ghosh et al., 2014; Fu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: Azoramide, an ER calcium modulator, has shown potent anti-diabetic efficacy.
source: KIRA6, an inhibitor of the UPR regulator IRE1, and azoramide, an ER calcium modulator, have shown potent anti-diabetic efficacy (Ghosh et al., 2014; Fu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: Sephin1, a PPP1R15A inhibitor, modulates PERK signalling and has been reported to exert neuroprotective effects in mouse models of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
source: Both Sephin1, a PPP1R15A inhibitor, and ISRIB, an eIF2B activator, modulate PERK signalling and have been reported to exert neuroprotective effects in mouse models of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and prion disease (Das et al., 2015; Halliday et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: ISRIB, an eIF2B activator, modulates PERK signalling and has been reported to exert neuroprotective effects in mouse models of prion disease.
source: Both Sephin1, a PPP1R15A inhibitor, and ISRIB, an eIF2B activator, modulate PERK signalling and have been reported to exert neuroprotective effects in mouse models of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and prion disease (Das et al., 2015; Halliday et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: 4-Phenylbutyrate (4PBA) and taurourso-deoxycholic acid (TUDCA) have been reported to function as chemical chaperones.
source: 4-Phenylbutyrate (4PBA) and taurourso-deoxycholic acid (TUDCA) have been reported to function as chemical chaperones and have shown therapeutic benefits for a wide variety of diseases, such as diabetes, ALS and Alzheimer's disease (Ozcan et al., 2006; Cudkowicz et al., 2009; Nunes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: 4PBA and TUDCA have shown therapeutic benefits for diabetes, ALS and Alzheimer's disease.
source: 4-Phenylbutyrate (4PBA) and taurourso-deoxycholic acid (TUDCA) have been reported to function as chemical chaperones and have shown therapeutic benefits for a wide variety of diseases, such as diabetes, ALS and Alzheimer's disease (Ozcan et al., 2006; Cudkowicz et al., 2009; Nunes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: The EUA-EGFP reporter cells can simultaneously monitor the activation of the three branches of the UPR with high sensitivity and specificity.
source: The EUA-EGFP reporter cells can simultaneously monitor the activation of the three branches of the UPR with high sensitivity and specificity using the specific ER stressor tunicamycin (Tm), an inhibitor of N-linked glycosylation (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The EUA-EGFP reporter assay has a signal-to-background ratio of 5.09 ± 1.28.
source: The EUA-EGFP reporter cells allowed us to perform 384-well HTS via a sensitive (signal-to-background ratio = 5.09 ± 1.28) and robust (Z' factor = 0.78 ± 0.06) homogeneous assay using a microplate reader (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental setup.

claim: The EUA-EGFP reporter assay has a Z' factor of 0.78 ± 0.06.
source: The EUA-EGFP reporter cells allowed us to perform 384-well HTS via a sensitive (signal-to-background ratio = 5.09 ± 1.28) and robust (Z' factor = 0.78 ± 0.06) homogeneous assay using a microplate reader (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental setup.

claim: 217,765 compounds were screened from the Drug Discovery Initiative at the University of Tokyo chemical library.
source: We screened the 217,765-compound chemical library from the Drug Discovery Initiative at the University of Tokyo.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the screening campaign.

claim: 1920 compounds were identified in the first screening with % EUA-EGFP inhibition greater than the average + 5 SD and % viability greater than the average + 3 SD.
source: We identified 1920 compounds for which the % EUA-EGFP inhibition was greater than the average + 5 SD of the Tm-treated control (hit cut-off = 37%) and the % viability was greater than the average + 3 SD of the Tm-treated control (hit cut-off = 78%) (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the screening data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: Four of the top 10 hit compounds share a common 2-phenylimidazo[2,1-b]benzothiazole scaffold.
source: A maximum common substructure search identified a common scaffold in 4 of 10 compounds: the 2-phenylimidazo[2,1-b]benzothiazole skeleton (shown in red) (Figure 1D and F).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Removal of the phenyl group at the R1 position completely abolished UPR inhibition.
source: Removal of the phenyl group at the R1 position completely abolished UPR inhibition, indicating that the phenyl group is necessary for potency.
evidence: This is supported by SAR data shown in Figure 2.

claim: IBT29 exhibited higher activity than IBT21.
source: IBT29 exhibited higher activity than IBT21 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: At 10 µM IBT21, Tm-induced UPR activation was inhibited 91.8% in 293A cells.
source: At 10 µM IBT21, Tm-induced UPR activation was inhibited 91.8% by IBT21 in 293A cells (Figure 3B–D), as well as in another human cell line, Hap1 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claim: IBT21 demonstrated an IC50 value of 0.95 μM in the high content image analysis.
source: IBT21 demonstrated an IC50 value of 0.95 μM, consistent with the IC50 (0.61 μM) obtained from the HTS assay (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: AZO showed an IC50 value of 86 μM in the high content image analysis.
source: However, compared with IBT21, AZO and 4PBA showed much higher IC50 values of 86 μM and greater than 5,000 μM, respectively (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: 4PBA showed an IC50 value greater than 5,000 μM in the high content image analysis.
source: However, compared with IBT21, AZO and 4PBA showed much higher IC50 values of 86 μM and greater than 5,000 μM, respectively (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: IBT21 suppressed Tm-induced activation of all three UPR branch reporters in a dose-dependent manner.
source: As expected, IBT21 suppressed the Tm-induced activation of all three reporters in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: The IC50 values for IBT21 on ERSE2, UPRE and AARE reporters were 0.24 μM, 0.33 μM and 0.46 μM, respectively.
source: Indeed, the IC50 values for ERSE2 (0.24 μM), UPRE (0.33 μM) and AARE (0.46 μM) were similar to that of EUA-EGFP (0.61 μM), producing a similar dose-response curve.
evidence: These are quantitative measurements from experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: IBT21 treatment abolished Tm-induced increases in ATF4, GADD34 and CHOP levels in a dose-dependent manner.
source: As expected, the levels of ATF4, GADD34 and CHOP, markers of PERK branch signalling, were increased by Tm, and IBT21 treatment abolished these increases in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 4D,E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: IBT21 decreased the levels of DNAJB9, a marker of IRE1 branch signalling, which were induced by Tm.
source: Additionally, IBT21 decreased the levels of DNAJB9, a marker of IRE1 branch signalling, and SEL1L and HERPUD1, markers of ATF6 branch signalling, which were induced by Tm.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: IBT21 decreased the levels of SEL1L and HERPUD1, markers of ATF6 branch signalling, which were induced by Tm.
source: Additionally, IBT21 decreased the levels of DNAJB9, a marker of IRE1 branch signalling, and SEL1L and HERPUD1, markers of ATF6 branch signalling, which were induced by Tm.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: AZO did not decrease any UPR markers induced by Tm.
source: By contrast, the UPR modulator AZO did not decrease any markers in the UPR by Tm, consistent with the previous report (Fu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 4D and cited literature.

claim: IBT21 works as a chemical chaperone rather than a UPR modulator.
source: These results indicated that IBT21 works as a chemical chaperone rather than a UPR modulator.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing effects on all three UPR branches and comparison with AZO.

claim: IBT21 does not affect the ability to induce UPR target genes.
source: These data show that IBT21 does not affect the ability to induce UPR target genes.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with overexpressed UPR transcription factors shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: IBT21 does not affect protein translation.
source: We evaluated that IBT21 does not affect protein translation.
evidence: This is supported by puromycin incorporation assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: IBT21 modestly reduced DTT-induced ER stress.
source: We showed that IBT21 modestly reduced DTT-induced ER stress by monitoring the activation of EUA-EGFP reporter cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: IBT21 could not suppress the induction of heat-shock response by heat shock.
source: In contrast, IBT21 could not suppress the induction of heat-shock response by heat shock (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: IBT21 prevented protein aggregation induced by Tm as measured by ProteoStat dye staining.
source: Quantification of the ProteoStat dye staining within cells revealed increased fluorescence intensity in the Tm-treated cells (2.29-fold of untreated (UT)) and MG132-treated cells (2.33-fold of UT), and lower fluorescence intensity in the cells co-treated with Tm and IBT21 (0.87-fold of UT), showing that IBT21 prevented protein aggregation induced by Tm (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by ProteoStat dye staining data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: IBT21 inhibited protein aggregation in an in vitro assay using human insulin at a concentration of 10 µM.
source: As expected, IBT21 and 4PBA inhibited protein aggregation, indicating a direct function as chemical chaperones, though the UPR modulator AZO did not (Figure 5C). Notably, IBT21 inhibited protein aggregation at a concentration of 10 µM, which is 100-fold lower than that of 4PBA.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro aggregation assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: IBT21 inhibits protein aggregation at a concentration 100-fold lower than that of 4PBA.
source: Notably, IBT21 inhibited protein aggregation at a concentration of 10 µM, which is 100-fold lower than that of 4PBA.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison based on in vitro aggregation assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: 4PBA inhibited protein aggregation in an in vitro assay using human insulin.
source: As expected, IBT21 and 4PBA inhibited protein aggregation, indicating a direct function as chemical chaperones, though the UPR modulator AZO did not (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro aggregation assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: AZO did not inhibit protein aggregation in an in vitro assay using human insulin.
source: As expected, IBT21 and 4PBA inhibited protein aggregation, indicating a direct function as chemical chaperones, though the UPR modulator AZO did not (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro aggregation assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The levels of BiP in the AGGREGATED fraction were increased by Tm treatment (3.1-fold of UT) and this increase was significantly suppressed by IBT21 treatment (1.7-fold of UT).
source: Compared with the levels of BiP in the INPUT fraction, the levels of BiP in the AGGREGATED fraction corresponding to misfolded or aggregated proteins in the ER were increased by Tm treatment (3.1-fold of UT), and this increase was significantly suppressed by IBT21 treatment (1.7-fold of UT) (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: 211 of 598 proteins (35.3%) in the AGGREGATED fraction were affected by Tm.
source: We found that 211 of 598 proteins (35.3%) were affected by Tm, and 125 of those 211 proteins (59.2%) were affected by IBT21 (IBT-SENSITIVE proteins), suggesting that IBT21 prevents Tm-induced protein misfolding (Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: 125 of 211 Tm-affected proteins (59.2%) were affected by IBT21 (IBT-SENSITIVE proteins).
source: We found that 211 of 598 proteins (35.3%) were affected by Tm, and 125 of those 211 proteins (59.2%) were affected by IBT21 (IBT-SENSITIVE proteins), suggesting that IBT21 prevents Tm-induced protein misfolding (Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Extracellular compartments were highly enriched in the IBT-SENSITIVE proteins based on Gene Ontology annotation.
source: Extracellular compartments were highly enriched in the category of cellular components (Figure 5H Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Protein folding was highly enriched in the category of biological function for IBT-SENSITIVE proteins.
source: In addition to ER client proteins, proteins required for proteostasis could also be affected by Tm and IBT21. As expected, protein folding was highly enriched in the category of biological function, as the representative proteins from the AGGREGATED fraction included the molecular chaperone HSPA5 and the ER folding enzyme PDIA4 (Figure 5G,I, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The activity of diazido-IBT21 was comparable to that of IBT21.
source: The activity of diazido-IBT21 was comparable to that of IBT21, and we used the more potent compound IBT22 as a competitor (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 1441 proteins were detected as IBT-BOUNDED proteins in the photoaffinity labeling experiment.
source: In total, 1441 proteins were detected as IBT-BOUNDED proteins and were classified with the following criteria: 1) 1.5-fold change in the probe-treated samples compared to the probe- and competitor-treated samples (competed) and 2) 1.5-fold change in the probe-treated samples compared to the UT samples (selective) (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 1205 proteins were categorized as Competed and Selective IBT-BOUNDED proteins.
source: The IBT-BOUNDED proteins were categorized into the following four groups: Competed and Selective (1205 proteins), Competed (11 proteins), Selective (185 proteins) and Non-Specific (40 proteins) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The Competed and Selective proteins were the majority (84%) of the IBT-BOUNDED proteins.
source: The Competed and Selective proteins were the majority (84%) of the IBT-BOUNDED proteins.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: 58 proteins were identified as Overlapped proteins observed in both the IBT-SENSITIVE proteins and the Competed and Selective proteins.
source: To characterize the IBT21-targeted proteins to corresponding chemical chaperone activity, we analyzed the Overlapped proteins observed in both the IBT-SENSITIVE proteins and the Competed and Selective proteins.
evidence: This is shown in the flow diagram in Figure 6F.

claim: The Overlapped proteins contained approximately 60% of the IBT-SENSITIVE proteins in each enriched GO group.
source: Nevertheless, the Overlapped proteins contained approximately 60% of the IBT-SENSITIVE proteins in each enriched GO group, indicating that the Competed and Selective proteins largely cover the IBT21-targeted proteins corresponding to chemical chaperone activity (Figure 6H).
evidence: This is supported by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Treatment with 1 µM IBT21 restored the cell growth inhibited by Tm up to 69.8% of the growth of the untreated cells.
source: Treatment with 1 µM IBT21 restored the cell growth inhibited by Tm up to 69.8% of the growth of the UT cells (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is supported by cell proliferation data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: Cell growth was significantly stimulated to 112.7 or 115.8% of that of UT cells by the addition of 5 or 10 μM IBT21, respectively, even in the presence of Tm.
source: Surprisingly, cell growth was significantly stimulated to 112.7 or 115.8% of that of UT cells by the addition of 5 or 10 μM IBT21, respectively, even in the presence of Tm.
evidence: This is supported by cell proliferation data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: 40 μM AZO treatment led to a significant but modest growth recovery up to 58.1% of that of the UT cells.
source: In contrast, 40 μM AZO treatment led to a significant but modest growth recovery up to 58.1% of that of the UT cells.
evidence: This is supported by cell proliferation data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: IBT21 treatment attenuated viability loss and cell death in a dose-dependent manner under ER stress conditions.
source: Consistent with the results of the proliferation assays, IBT21 treatment attenuated viability loss and cell death in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This is supported by ATP and LDH assay data shown in Figure 7C and D.

claim: 5 μM IBT21 treatment restored the cell growth inhibition caused by mutant PrP overexpression.
source: Overexpression of mut PrP inhibited cell proliferation, and 5 μM IBT21 treatment restored the cell growth inhibition caused by mutant PrP overexpression (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is supported by cell proliferation data shown in Figure 7E and F.

claim: The recovery of viability loss by IBT21 treatment in the mutant PrP-overexpressing cells was confirmed by CellTiter-Glo assay.
source: Consistent with the results from the proliferation assays using the high content imaging system, the recovery of viability loss by IBT21 treatment in the mutant PrP-overexpressing cells was also confirmed by a biochemical assay with CellTiter-Glo.
evidence: This is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: IBTs are promising scaffolds for chemical chaperones.
source: The observed effects cannot be explained by a simple mechanism because these compounds have a planar conjugated ring system similar to many DNA intercalators; however, IBTs are promising scaffolds for chemical chaperones.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective experimental data presented in the study.

claim: IBT21 acted as a pharmacological chaperone.
source: Structurally, IBT21 was not particularly similar to osmoprotectants, and IBT21 was observed to preferably bind to unfolded or misfolded proteins in combined analyses such as the ER stress-induced aggregated protein profile and the IBT21-targeted protein profile. Therefore, we considered that IBT21 acted as a pharmacological chaperone.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis and binding data.

claim: The IBT21 core possesses hydrophobicity comparable to that of 4PBA and TUDCA.
source: The IBT21 core possesses hydrophobicity comparable to that of 4PBA and TUDCA, which are known to be hydrophobic compounds.
evidence: This is based on chemical structure analysis and comparison.

claim: 4PBA and TUDCA are the only two pharmacological chaperones for proteotoxins approved by the FDA for human use.
source: Currently, 4PBA and TUDCA are the only two pharmacological chaperones for proteotoxins approved by the FDA for human use.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FDA-approved drugs.

claim: IBT21 shows much higher chaperone-like activity than 4PBA.
source: Notably, IBT21 shows much higher chaperone-like activity than 4PBA.
evidence: This is supported by comparative experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 5C.

claim: Pharmacological chaperones for proteotoxin have one of three mechanisms of action: preventing protein aggregation by masking the aggregation-prone region (group I), increasing the folding rate by stabilizing the folding transition state (group II) or decreasing the misfolding rate by stabilizing the native state (group III).
source: In theory, pharmacological chaperones for proteotoxin have one of the following three mechanisms of action: preventing protein aggregation by masking the aggregation-prone region (group I), increasing the folding rate by stabilizing the folding transition state (group II) or decreasing the misfolding rate by stabilizing the native state (group III).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chemical chaperone mechanisms.

claim: IBT21 directly prevents protein aggregation in an in vitro aggregation inhibition assay.
source: We demonstrated that IBT21 directly prevents protein aggregation in an in vitro aggregation inhibition assay, but the second and third mechanisms remain elusive.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro aggregation assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Heat shock response is not influenced by IBT21.
source: Notably, heat shock response is not influenced by IBT21.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Alagille et al. designed and synthesized a series of 2-aryl-imidazo[2,1-b]benzothiazoles by a combination of the benzothiazole motif and the 2-arylimidazo motif from two potent β-amyloid imaging agents, PIB and IMPY.
source: Alagille et al. designed and synthesized a series of 2-aryl-imidazo[2,1-b]benzothiazoles by a combination of the benzothiazole motif and the 2-arylimidazo motif from two potent β-amyloid imaging agents, PIB and IMPY, respectively (Alagille et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: 11C-labelled IBTs have high in vitro and in vivo binding affinities for β-amyloid aggregates.
source: Yousefi et al. demonstrated that 11C-labelled IBTs have high in vitro and in vivo binding affinities for β-amyloid aggregates (Alagille et al., 2011) and that 18F-labelled IBTs allow high-contrast PET imaging of β-amyloids in Alzheimer's disease model mice (Yousefi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: 18F-labelled IBTs allow high-contrast PET imaging of β-amyloids in Alzheimer's disease model mice.
source: Yousefi et al. demonstrated that 11C-labelled IBTs have high in vitro and in vivo binding affinities for β-amyloid aggregates (Alagille et al., 2011) and that 18F-labelled IBTs allow high-contrast PET imaging of β-amyloids in Alzheimer's disease model mice (Yousefi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: IBT21 could be effective for PET and SPECT imaging of ER stress-related diseases.
source: Together with our results, these findings indicate that IBT21 could be effective for PET and SPECT imaging of ER stress-related diseases.
evidence: This is speculation based on the chemical properties of IBT21 and cited literature on related compounds.

claim: Neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Huntington disease and prion disease are caused by the accumulation of neurotoxic protein aggregates.
source: It is generally accepted that neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Huntington disease and prion disease are caused by the accumulation of neurotoxic protein aggregates, and chemical chaperones have the potential to separate these neurotoxic aggregates.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: TMAO was first applied for preventing PrPSC formation in vitro as a chemical chaperone in the late 1990s.
source: In the case of prion disease, the osmoprotectant TMAO was first applied for preventing PrPSC formation in vitro as a chemical chaperone in the late 1990 s (Tatzelt et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: PrPSC toxicity was reported to cause ER stress by increasing the intracellular calcium released from the ER.
source: PrPSC toxicity was reported to cause ER stress by increasing the intracellular calcium released from the ER (Hetz et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: A reduction in the levels of the ER molecular chaperone BiP accelerates prion pathogenesis in vivo.
source: Indeed, a reduction in the levels of the ER molecular chaperone BiP accelerates prion pathogenesis in vivo, indicating that the accumulation of the misfolded form of PrP in the ER is a key event in prion propagation (Park et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: Prion replication has been shown to cause sustained UPR induction with persistent eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: Prion replication has been shown to cause sustained UPR induction with persistent eIF2α phosphorylation (Moreno et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of PERK by GSK2606414 mitigated neurodegeneration and clinical prion disease in mice.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of PERK by the compound GSK2606414 mitigated neurodegeneration and clinical prion disease in mice (Moreno et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: The best treatment regimen for prion disease may involve a combination of compounds that fine-tune protein synthesis and reduce protein aggregates.
source: In this study, we demonstrated that IBT21 presents the most effective treatment effect and that the best treatment regimen may involve a combination of compounds, some of which fine-tune protein synthesis, such as GSK2606414, and others that reduce protein aggregates, such as the chemical chaperone IBT21.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental results and cited literature.
